title: Breathing mode inducing dynamical pairing in Kagome materials
authors: Debmalya Chakraborty, Anushree Datta, Jorge Cayao
abstract: The breathing mode in Kagome materials is a structural modulation that breaks inversion symmetry and has been shown to be a crucial source for intriguing phases in the normal state. In this work, we carry out a full classification of superconducting symmetries in kagome superconductors and demonstrate the emergence of odd-frequency dynamical Cooper pairs entirely driven by the breathing mode. We then show that odd-frequency spin-singlet Cooper pairs can be realized by controlling the breathing mode in kagome lattices with conventional spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductivity. Since odd-frequency pairing is intrinsically nonlocal in time, our results put forward the breathing mode for designing dynamical Cooper pairs in kagome materials.
summary: This work theoretically investigates how a breathing mode structural distortion in Kagome materials can stabilize exotic superconducting phases. The authors classify possible pair symmetries and demonstrate that this specific distortion induces odd-frequency, dynamical Cooper pairs. This finding provides a mechanism for designing unconventional superconductivity using lattice engineering.
main_problem: To classify superconducting symmetries in Kagome superconductors and demonstrate the emergence of odd-frequency dynamical Cooper pairs driven by structural distortions.
main_result: The breathing mode induces odd-frequency spin-singlet Cooper pairs, which are entirely dependent on the structural distortion breaking inversion symmetry.
method: Full classification of superconducting symmetries using anomalous Green's function symmetry analysis and self-consistent solution of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian.
model_or_system:
The system is Kagome materials studied under a 'breathing mode' structural distortion ($t_a 
eq t_b$). The superconductivity is modeled using an onsite spin-singlet pairing approach within the Nambu Green's function formalism.
key_observables: Superconducting pair amplitudes, symmetry classes (e.g., OSEO), and gap opening in band structures.
important_parameters:
The structural distortion parameter ($t_a 
eq t_b$), chemical potential ($\mu$), and frequency/momentum dependence of pairing functions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes onsite spin-singlet superconductivity, though the resulting odd-frequency pairs imply sublattice symmetry breaking is key.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows pair amplitude dependence on imaginary time; Figure 2 compares band structures with and without distortion (showing gap opening); Figure 3 illustrates spectral function and OSEO pair amplitudes vs. frequency/momentum.
paper_structure: The paper first classifies all possible superconducting symmetries in the Kagome lattice, then analyzes how the breathing mode breaks inversion symmetry to stabilize a specific odd-frequency pairing state ($E^{(2)}_2$), which is shown to be non-local in time.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the concept of dynamical pairing driven by structural modulation and its connection to unconventional superconductivity has parallels with engineered quantum systems where lattice vibrations or external fields induce novel many-body states.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
